description: HYBRID trailing update that removes the host sync + reorder WITHOUT replacing cuBLAS (which beats custom GEMM 3x — briefs 5/26/27). Currently n=512/1024 classify -> host n_well.item() -> gather well matrices contiguous -> 2 cuBLAS GEMMs (TF32 well group, FP32 ill group) -> inverse-permute. Instead: run the trailing GEMM (W=V^T C; C-=V T^T W) in TF32 over the WHOLE batch in ONE cuBLAS strided-batched call (no gather, no host n_well) — this is correct for the well-conditioned majority; THEN a small device kernel re-does ONLY the ill matrices (band/rowscale/mixed-ill, flagged by the existing device classify) in FP32 in place (recompute their trailing block at FP32 and overwrite). Ill matrices are the minority so the FP32 correction is cheap, and the bulk stays on fast cuBLAS TF32. Removes the ~448us reorder gather + the per-panel host .item() sync (the real overhead) while keeping cuBLAS GEMM throughput. Reuse brief-27's device per-matrix-flag infra. Default stream only; do NOT write or obfuscate the substring 'stream' incl. comments. FP32 panel. Keep n!=512/1024 as parent.

HYBRID built + CORRECT: whole-batch cuBLAS TF32 trailing GEMM over the WHOLE batch (no gather, no n_well.item()) + a custom device kernel (ill_trailing_fp32_kernel) that re-does ONLY the ill matrices (device float flag wellf, 1=well/0=ill from the existing classifier) at FP32 into a side buffer, then ill_copyback overwrites C[ill]. Batch NEVER reordered; the .item() sync + argsort + full-batch gather/scatter are ALL GONE (nsys n512mixed: NO gather/scatter/radixSort kernels). Validate PASS 22 tests + kernelguard CLEAN + 3 guards (diff_correctness/invariance fraction+position/offgrid) CLEAN. Two stride bugs fixed en route: (a) Y=T^T W needs sum_{l<=a} T[l][a] W[l] (had T@W); (b) V/T are slices of (B,n,nb) workspaces so batch stride is n*nb not m*cb -- pass V.stride/T.stride/C.stride explicitly (panel-0 happened to alias correct when m==n). RESULT in heavy slow-mode contention (n2048 anchor shape5 32185 == parent 32116, same level): geomean 11039 vs parent 9032 = 1.22x WORSE. SPLIT verdict: ALL-WELL shapes IMPROVED ~8-13% (shape3 n512 17675->15448, shape9 17536->15315, shape10 17673->15438, shape4 n1024 21005->19344, shape11 21019->19363) -- removing the .item() the parent still pays on the all-well branch is a real win. But the MIXED shapes BLEW UP: shape7 n512mixed 21307->77975 (3.66x), shape8 n1024mixed 23359->124752 (5.34x). nsys n512mixed: ill_trailing_fp32_kernel=65.8pct (72.4ms), panel=21.1pct, whole-batch TF32 GEMMs=11.5pct, ill_copyback=1.5pct, classify 0.1pct. ROOT CAUSE: my naive custom FP32 GEMM (each warp owns 1 output col, re-reads all of V, zero reuse) is ~14x slower than cuBLAS on the ill 17pct -- far worse than brief-27's 2x. The reorder removal is CONFIRMED and the all-well win is real, but the custom FP32 ill kernel must get MUCH faster (or use a 2nd cuBLAS bmm over gathered ill matrices). Next: make ill-correction fast.

STRATEGY A: replace trial-1's slow custom FP32 kernel with a SECOND cuBLAS bmm over the GATHERED ill matrices. Per panel: gather Vi/Ti/Ci=index_select(ill_idx) of the ill minority, whole-batch TF32 bmm in place (well majority done), then FP32 cuBLAS bmm correction on the gathered ill, index_copy_ back. ill_idx via ONE torch.nonzero(~well) (the parent paid an equivalent .item()); NO argsort, NO full-batch reorder gather/scatter. Validate PASS 22 tests + kernelguard + 3 guards CLEAN. RESULT (same contention: n2048 anchor shape5 32200 == parent 32116): geomean 9356 vs parent 9032 = 1.036x WORSE -- but MUCH better than trial-1 (11039). MIXED shapes fixed from catastrophic to modest: shape7 n512mixed 77975->25255 (now +18.5pct vs parent 21307); shape8 n1024mixed 124752->29932 (+28.1pct vs parent 23359). cuBLAS-on-gathered-ill is ~3-4x faster than my custom kernel on the ill work. KEY REGRESSION vs trial-1: the ALL-WELL shapes LOST trial-1's ~12pct win and snapped back to PARENT level (shape3 17681==parent 17675, shape4 21011==parent 21005, shape9/10/11 all ~parent) because torch.nonzero(~well) reintroduces a HOST SYNC that drains the pipeline -- trial-1's float-flag path had ZERO sync and the CPU ran all ~16 panels' launches ahead, hiding launch latency (that bubble removal WAS the 12pct). Contention identical across runs (shape2 n352 2887 both; shape5 32184/32200). VERDICT: the geomean loss is now ONLY the 2 mixed shapes (+18/+28pct); the 5 all-well shapes are neutral. To WIN: need BOTH trial-1's sync-free all-well win (0.88^5) AND trial-2's cuBLAS-quality mixed (1.18,1.28) => projected geomean ~0.98 (2pct win). But the two are in tension: sync-free forbids the gather (needs nonzero size). Next: sync-free path with a FAST device FP32 ill correction (make trial-1's kernel ~4x not 14x).

SYNC-FREE float-flag path RESTORED + a tiled FP32 ill kernel (one CTA/matrix, V staged in SMEM once and reused across strips, C strip-mined SW=16 to fit m=1024 at 196KB SMEM, all from SMEM). Unit-test: bit-exact (rel 0.0) vs FP32 cuBLAS reference; well-skip confirmed. Validate PASS 22 tests + kernelguard + 3 guards CLEAN. THIS RUN ~1.49x MORE CONTENDED than the parent baseline (anchor n2048 shape5 47976 vs 32116; n352 shape2 4260 vs 2887; n4096 102013 vs 68280 -- all ~1.49x), so use CONTENTION-INVARIANT RATIOS vs shape5. ALL-WELL shapes IMPROVED relative (sync removal win restored): shape3 ratio 0.4615 vs parent 0.5503 (~16pct faster rel), shape9 0.4588 vs 0.546, shape4 0.5889 vs 0.654, shape11 0.5890 vs 0.654. But MIXED still CATASTROPHIC: shape7 n512mixed ratio 1.4262 vs parent 0.6634 (2.15x worse rel); shape8 n1024mixed ratio 5.023 vs parent 0.7274 (6.9x worse rel, raw 240990 -- WORSE than trial-1!). ROOT CAUSE: at n1024 m=1024 the one-CTA-per-matrix design has only ~10 ill CTAs on 148 SMs (massively under-occupied) AND each output is a SERIAL length-1024 SMEM reduction -- the per-matrix serial m-reduction is the killer; SW=16/196KB caps at 1 CTA/SM. The V-in-SMEM reuse helped n512 vs trial-1 (shape7 78k->68k) but the structure is fundamentally wrong for low-batch-large-n. CONFIRMS brief-27's finding from a 2nd angle: NO custom FP32 device kernel I write beats cuBLAS on this trailing GEMM. CORE TENSION now fully measured: sync-free => all-well +12-16pct win but custom-kernel mixed is catastrophic; cuBLAS-gather (trial 2) => mixed decent (+18-28pct) but nonzero sync kills the all-well win. Next: cuBLAS-gather (Strategy A) but HIDE the nonzero sync behind the clone + first panel_factor so the GPU never idles -- recover the all-well win AND keep cuBLAS mixed quality.

DEFERRED-SYNC gather hybrid: Strategy A (whole-batch cuBLAS TF32 + 2nd FP32 cuBLAS bmm over index_select'd ill minority + index_copy_ back), but the ONE nonzero(~well) host sync is DEFERRED until after H.clone()+first panel_factor are enqueued, so the GPU stays busy through the CPU round-trip. Validate PASS 22 tests + kernelguard + 3 guards CLEAN. THIS RUN ~1.5x contended (anchor n2048 shape5 48269 vs parent 32116 => f=1.503; shape2 n352 4259 vs 2886 => f=1.476; shape6 102000 vs 68280 => f=1.494). CONTENTION-NORMALIZED geomean (13373/f): ~8898-9061 vs parent 9032 = roughly BREAK-EVEN to ~1.5pct better (best NET result so far; trial-2 was clearly 3.6pct worse). Per-shape ratios vs shape5: MIXED shape7 0.7062 vs parent 0.6634 (+6.4pct rel), shape8 0.8757 vs 0.7274 (+20.4pct rel) -- better than trial-2's +18/+28. ALL-WELL shapes 0.5456/0.5434/0.6652/0.6653 ~= PARENT (0.55/0.55/0.654/0.654), i.e. NEUTRAL -- the deferred sync did NOT recover trial-1/3's sync-free +16pct all-well win (trial-3 sync-free all-well ratio 0.4615 vs this 0.5456 = trial-3 16pct faster). So deferring the sync behind clone+panel0 hides only part of it: for the small all-well panels the GPU catches up to the sync point and idles. CORE TENSION CONFIRMED+QUANTIFIED: sync-free => +16pct all-well but custom-kernel mixed catastrophic; cuBLAS-gather => good mixed but the (even deferred) nonzero sync costs all-well ~16pct. Trial-4 is the best blend (~break-even) because cuBLAS mixed + only-partial all-well loss. OPEN: cut the per-panel index_select/index_copy_ overhead on the low-batch n1024 mixed (shape8 the laggard, B=60); or a sync-free 1-bit 'any-ill' device flag to pick all-well-fast vs gather; or reduce the deferred-sync bubble further (enqueue 2 panels before nonzero).

TWO-PASS hybrid: pass1 = whole-batch cuBLAS TF32 QR over ALL B (sync-free); nonzero(~well) sync hidden behind pass1; pass2 = independent FP32 cuBLAS QR of the gathered ill subset A[ill_idx], overwriting its (H,tau) rows (gather/scatter ONCE, not per panel). Validate PASS 22 + kernelguard + 3 guards CLEAN. THIS RUN f~1.48 (shape5 47446/32116, shape2 4260/2886, shape6 103688/68280). CONTENTION-INVARIANT geomean ratio (via shape5): (13848/47446)/(9032/32116)=1.0378 => 3.8pct WORSE than parent; WORSE than trial-4. nsys n512mixed ROOT CAUSE: panel_factor 54.8pct with 32 INSTANCES (vs 16 in parent/trial-4) -- two-pass RE-FACTORS the ill matrices' panels (pass1 does all B, pass2 re-does ill), and the panel is the dominant cost, so duplicating it for ill loses. The FP32 ill trailing (cutlass simt_sgemm) is only ~5pct and gather/index_copy ~0.8pct (gather-once IS cheap, as hoped) -- but the panel duplication dwarfs that saving. shape8 n1024mixed 53870 (f1.48) >> trial-4's 42268 (f1.5) confirms. VERDICT: two-pass is WORSE than trial-4's per-panel cuBLAS gather because trial-4 shares the panel across all B (panel once). Per-panel gather (trial 4) remains the best structure. Per contention-invariant ratios, trial-4=0.9852 (1.5pct better via shape5), trial-5=1.0378, trial-2=1.0331. CONFIRMED: the panel must run ONCE for the whole batch; the ill FP32 work must be a per-panel TRAILING correction (cheap cuBLAS), NOT a full re-factor. Reverting to trial-4's per-panel-gather structure for the final; will also strip the now-dead custom ill_trailing_fp32/ill_copyback CUDA kernels.

CLEANED FINAL = trial-4 structure (per-panel cuBLAS-gather ill correction, deferred nonzero sync) + removed the dead custom ill_trailing_fp32/ill_copyback CUDA kernels and the dead n_well reorder-split branch in _blocked_qr. Validate PASS 22 + kernelguard + 3 guards CLEAN. THIS RUN AT CLEAN CONTENTION (f~1.00: anchor shape5 32140 vs parent 32116, shape2 2889 vs 2886, shape6 67975 vs 68280) => DIRECT same-contention A/B vs parent. RESULT: geomean 9203 vs parent 9032 = 1.019x WORSE (1.9pct). Per-shape (direct): ALL-WELL slight win shape3 17459 vs 17675 (-1.2pct), shape9 17281 vs 17536 (-1.5pct), shape10 17430 vs 17673 (-1.4pct), shape4 20960 vs 21005 (-0.2pct), shape11 20960 vs 21019 (-0.3pct). MIXED worse: shape7 n512mixed 23052 vs 21307 (+8.2pct), shape8 n1024mixed 28333 vs 23359 (+21.3pct). MEASURED NEGATIVE. nsys n512mixed ROOT CAUSE: panel 39.3pct (16 inst, NO duplication), whole-batch TF32 GEMMs ~29pct, FP32 ill simt_sgemm ~5.7pct (CHEAP), but the PER-PANEL ill gather (_scatter_gather 3.7pct=667us) + scatter (index_copy 3.6pct=644us) = ~7.3pct/1.3ms -- MORE than the parent's SINGLE full-batch reorder (~448us). So removing the once-only reorder and replacing it with 15x small per-panel ill gathers is a NET LOSS: the parent's 'reorder once, slice free every panel' is genuinely efficient. The deferred sync only recovered ~1pct of the ~13pct sync-free all-well win (sync-free measured at f~1.0 in trial-1 15448 vs trial-2 17680). VERDICT: the hybrid CANNOT beat the parent's gather-split on this HW -- per-panel ill gather > one full reorder, and the ill FP32 work CANNOT go sync-free without a custom GEMM (briefs 5/26/27 + my trials 1/3: custom GEMM is far slower). The brief's core mechanism (whole-batch TF32 + ill FP32 correction, no reorder) is BUILT, CORRECT, and MEASURED across 6 trials; it lands ~1.9pct short of the parent. OPEN: batch-size-routed (per-panel hybrid only for large-batch n512 where reorder is dear, parent reorder for small-batch n1024); or a fast sync-free split-K custom FP32 GEMM to fill SMs at low batch.

BRIEF BUILT, CORRECT, EXHAUSTIVELY MEASURED across 6 trials. The hybrid (whole-batch cuBLAS TF32 trailing GEMM + FP32 re-do of ONLY the ill matrices, NO full-batch reorder) is implemented and CORRECT (every trial: 22 tests + kernelguard + 3 guards CLEAN; invariance fraction/position sweeps confirm per-matrix routing without reorder). The full-batch argsort/gather/scatter reorder IS removed (nsys confirms no reorder kernels). FINAL HEAD 557e64c12 = per-panel cuBLAS-gather ill correction with the nonzero sync deferred behind clone+first-panel; dead custom kernels + dead n_well reorder-split branch stripped.

VERDICT: the hybrid lands ~1.9pct SHORT of the parent's gather-split at CLEAN contention (trial-6 direct same-contention A/B: geomean 9203 vs parent 9032, f~1.00 anchors matched within 0.1pct). MEASURED NEGATIVE, as the brief anticipated. Per-shape (direct): all-well shapes ~-1 to -1.5pct (slight win), mixed shapes +8.2pct (n512mixed) and +21.3pct (n1024mixed).

WHY IT CANNOT BEAT THE PARENT (airtight, profile-backed):
- The BIG all-well win (+12.6pct: trial-1 shape3 15448 vs parent 17675 at f~1.0) requires ZERO host sync in custom_kernel -- eval.py's timed repeat LOOP pipelines consecutive repeats' launches only when nothing syncs; ANY .item()/nonzero/all per call serializes the repeats and gives back ~11 of those 12.6 points (trials 2/4/5/6 all land at parent-level all-well despite deferring the sync; sync-free trial-1 uniquely kept it).
- ZERO sync FORBIDS the cuBLAS gather (the ill COUNT is needed to size the gather -> nonzero -> sync). So sync-free forces a CUSTOM device FP32 GEMM for the ill correction.
- Custom device GEMMs are far slower than cuBLAS on this small-K (cb=32) trailing GEMM: trial-1 naive (per-col, no V reuse) = 14x cuBLAS -> n512mixed catastrophic 78k; trial-3 tiled (V in SMEM, one CTA/matrix) still bad and WORSE at n1024 (per-matrix serial length-1024 reduction, ~10 ill CTAs on 148 SMs = under-occupied) -> n1024mixed 241k. This reproduces brief-27's finding (it spent 7 trials and even tuned WMMA only reached 2x cuBLAS).
- WITH the gather (sync), mixed is decent but two costs remain: (a) the sync kills the all-well win (above); (b) PER-PANEL ill gather/scatter costs MORE than the parent's once-only reorder. nsys n512mixed: panel 39pct, whole-batch TF32 29pct, FP32 ill sgemm only ~5.7pct (cheap!), but per-panel _scatter_gather 3.7pct + index_copy 3.6pct = ~1.3ms > the parent's single 448us reorder. nsys n1024mixed: panel 73.5pct (B=60 work-starved), indexSelect 7.6pct + index_copy 2.3pct over 32 panels = the +21pct drag. The parent's 'reorder ONCE, slice free every panel' is genuinely efficient.
- TWO-PASS (trial 5: whole-batch TF32 then independent FP32 re-factor of the gathered ill subset) avoids per-panel gather BUT DUPLICATES the dominant panel for the ill subset (nsys: 32 panel instances incl ill re-factor) -> 3.8pct WORSE than trial-4. So the ill fix MUST be a per-panel trailing correction, not a re-factor.

TRIAL ARC (all CLEAN, contention-invariant via the n2048/n352 anchors): t1 sync-free+naive-custom geomean 11039 (catastrophic mixed, +12.6pct all-well); t2 cuBLAS-gather+top-sync 9356 (mixed +18/28, all-well neutral); t3 sync-free+tiled-custom ~10300-norm (mixed still bad); t4 cuBLAS-gather+deferred-sync ~break-even-to-1.5pct-better (best blend); t5 two-pass +3.8pct; t6 cleaned t4 = -1.9pct at clean contention (final).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (manager to weigh -- NONE closed):
1. SYNC-FREE split-K custom FP32 GEMM for the ill correction: split the m-reduction across CTAs (B_ill * K CTAs) to fill SMs at low batch (n1024 B=60), with register tiling -- the one un-exhausted lever that could keep the sync-free +12.6pct all-well win AND make mixed acceptable. CAVEAT: brief-27 spent 7 trials and concluded custom GEMM tops out ~2x cuBLAS, so this is a long shot the manager may judge not worth it.
2. BATCH-SIZE ROUTING: per-panel hybrid only for LARGE batch (n512 B=640, where the reorder is dearest ~448us) and the PARENT's reorder-split for SMALL batch (n1024 B=60, reorder cheap). Removes the +21pct n1024mixed drag; my arithmetic still nets ~break-even because n512mixed +8pct outweighs the small all-well wins -- needs a measured check.
3. Cut the per-panel index overhead: gather Vi/Ti/Ci in ONE fused indexed copy, or use a custom masked-gather kernel; reduces the 1.3ms (n512) / 1.66ms (n1024) index cost toward the parent's single 448us.
4. The panel is now 39-73pct of the mixed shapes and the universal co-limiter (brief-0/23/35 territory); any panel speedup would shrink the trailing/index fraction this brief targets.
